results.title: at 1,000 rows, list rendered, unthrottled: every operation of every variant finishes Svelte's DOM update within 16.7 ms (style and layout not included)
at 100,000 rows with a $derived total, assign + the first $derived full read costs at least 10x more with $state than with $state.raw, and uses 50+ MB more heap
$state.raw mutated in place: the screen does not change; a new array shows the pushed row but NOT the edited field; only a new object for that row shows it
$state creates proxies lazily: assigning 100,000 unread rows is under 5 ms and adds under 1 MB; the first full read adds 50+ MB and is slower than the second
hybrid: the first edit of a row swaps in a $state proxy (new array); later edits change only that row (same array) and update the screen
at 100,000 rows (windowed list), repeated edits of one row: hybrid is at least 3x faster than an immutable copy with $state.raw
a $state array does not return the objects you put in: identity checks fail, writes through it do not reach the original
$state.snapshot of 10,000 rows is at least 2x slower than structuredClone of the same plain rows, and snapshotting an unread $state list is slower still
server render: $state and $state.raw compile to the same server code, and render 10,000 rows within 15% of each other
rendering 10,000 rows (keyed each, full list): $state takes at least 2x as long as $state.raw
sorting 100,000 rows (data page): on $state, both in place and as toSorted + reassignment, is at least 3x slower than toSorted on $state.raw
at 10,000 rows with a $derived total and 4x CPU throttling, one edit on $state takes at least 5x as long as on $state.raw
windowed list (50 of 100,000 rows rendered): an edit on $state is no slower than on $state.raw, but a sort on $state is at least 3x slower
hybrid: a promoted row replaced by a new object with the same id is promoted again on its next edit, and the screen updates
